$comment: Neutral description of the Duet 3 CAN message formats. This file is the single source of truth;
(C#) are generated from it by tools/CanMessageGenerator.
Layout rules (verified against g++ __attribute__((packed)) on little-endian targets):
- a bit cursor runs through the struct; a bitfield is placed at the cursor and advances it by its
width, with no padding and no regard for the declared storage type (bitfields may straddle both
byte and storage-unit boundaries, and consecutive groups of different storage types pack together);
- a non-bitfield member rounds the cursor up to the next byte boundary before being placed;
- the struct size is the cursor rounded up to a whole number of bytes.
Field order therefore matters and must not be changed without bumping the message type.

structs.name: CanTiming
doc: CAN bit timing parameters, declared in CANlib's CanSettings.h.

expression language does not cover, so they are hand-written in the other half of the partial.

structs.name: CanMessageMultipleDrivesRequest
doc: Set a per-driver parameter for multiple drivers. The meaning of the values depends on the message type:
- motor currents: currents in mA;
- microstepping: microstepping (bits 0-8) and interpolation enable (bit 15);
- standstill current percentages: the percentages;
- driver states: 0 = disabled, 1 = idle, 2 = active.

instantiations.doc: Legacy: the uint16 forms of microstepping and standstill current were retired (see unused_was_setMicrostepping and unused_was_setStandstillCurrentFactor). CANlib still declares this arm of the union, so the type is kept, but nothing sends it.

structs.name: DriverStateControl
doc: Driver state sent in a CanMessageMultipleDrivesRequest. The meaning of idlePercent is:
- if the mode is driverIdle then the top 8 bits are the idle current percent, to match the earlier version of this struct;
- if the mode is driverDisabled then all 12 bits are the delay in milliseconds between re-engaging the brake and disabling the motor;
- if the mode is driverEnabled then all 12 bits are the delay in milliseconds between enabling the motor and disengaging the brake.

structs.name: CanMessageHeaterTuningCommand
doc: Enter tuning mode (used by M303). This causes the heater to cycle between two temperatures, reporting data at the end of each cycle.
If just the 'on' bit is set, we are asking for heater tuning to start.
If 'on' and 'calibrate' are both set, we are asking for calibration to start.
If just 'calibrate' is set, we are asking whether calibration has completed.

doc: The standard reply used by many calls. It carries a GCodeResult, some text, and in some cases 8 bits of
additional information. It can be split into multiple fragments so that the text is not constrained to 60 characters.
The layout of requestId and resultCode is common to more than one reply type.

doc: Result of attempting to process a G-code command.
Mirrors GCodeResult in CANlib's GCodeResult.h. The value travels on the wire as the 4-bit
resultCode of a standard reply, so it has to keep CANlib's numbering.

values.name: notFinished
values.doc: we haven't finished processing this command

values.name: ok
values.doc: we have finished processing this code in the current state, and if the GCodeState is 'normal' then we have finished it completely

values.name: warning
values.doc: the command succeeded but a warning was generated

values.name: warningNotSupported
values.doc: the command is not supported, but for this command we issue a warning not an error

values.name: error
values.doc: general error, the reason will be written to the associated reply buffer

values.name: errorNotSupported
values.doc: this command is not supported, and we treat it as an error because it's an important command

values.name: notSupportedInCurrentMode
values.doc: this command is supported in a different mode (FDM/Laser/CNC)

values.name: stopped
values.doc: we are halted because of an emergency stop

values.name: badOrMissingParameter
values.doc: a critical parameter is missing or has a bad value

values.name: remoteInternalError
values.doc: only used if CAN expansion is supported - can be sent by expansion boards, so don't change its number!

values.name: waitingForAckSoIgnored
values.doc: we are waiting for a message box to be acknowledged so the command has been ignored

values.name: noCanBuffer
values.doc: only used if CAN expansion is supported - we failed to allocate a CAN buffer to send a message to an expansion board

values.name: canResponseTimeout
values.doc: only used if CAN expansion is supported - timed out waiting for a response to a CAN message - the associated reply buffer may contain more info

enums.name: FirmwareFlashErrorCode

values.name: blockReceiveTimeout
values.doc: bootloader requested a firmware block from the master but didn't receive a reply

values.name: noFile
values.doc: bootloader requested firmware but the master responded that it didn't have the requested file

values.name: badOffset
values.doc: master reported that the file offset requested by the bootloader is out of range

values.name: hostOther
values.doc: master reported it was unable to supply the requested block for some other reason

values.name: noMemory
values.doc: bootloader ran out of RAM

values.name: flashInitFailed
values.doc: failed to initialise flash memory

values.name: unlockFailed
values.doc: failed to unlock flash memory

values.name: eraseFailed
values.doc: failed to erase flash memory

values.name: writeFailed
values.doc: failed to write flash memory

values.name: lockFailed
values.doc: failed to lock flash memory

values.name: vinTooLow
values.doc: expansion board was asked to update the bootloader but VIN is too low to do that safely

values.name: unknownBoard
values.doc: bootloader failed to identify the board type

values.name: vAssertCalled
values.doc: assertion failure in the bootloader

values.name: noTimeSyncMessageSeen
values.doc: bootloader didn't hear a clock message at any of the standard speeds (added for new bootloader)
